chunks: From him, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who gave a slave a female slave-servant as payment for a specified term. Later, the owner said to him, 'I cannot find a female slave-servant; take the value of your female slave-servant today and a slave.' He said, 'He takes only his female slave-servant or the slave he gave at first; nothing is added to it.'

key_terms.بِوَصِيفٍ: With a female slave-servant (used as payment/installment)
key_terms.لاَ يَزْدَادُ عَلَيْهِ شَيْئاً: Nothing is added to it (no increase/substitution)
key_terms.وَرِقاً: A slave (male or female, used here as principal debt)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a debtor cannot repay a specific item given as debt with its monetary value?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the nature of *Qard* (loan) in kind, establishing that the debtor must return the exact species and quality of the item originally borrowed, rather than its current market value or a substitute. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for differentiating between a simple loan and a sale with deferred payment, ensuring that no 'increase' (*Ziyadah*) occurs unless agreed upon, thereby preventing hidden usury (*Riba*). The hadith underscores the principle of strict equivalence in debt repayment, a key concept in *Fiqh al-Mu'amalat* as detailed in Shaykh al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
